meta.audience: A firefighter/EMT on an annual refresher, where part of the record is the department's own written assessment.
meta.why: Two calls run in the simulator, the department's written assessment run by the host, and a debrief station at the end. The external node is the whole reason this flow exists: the host owns the assessment and this side owns the calls, and neither pretends to run the other.
meta.hostNotes: On reaching `ext-assessment` the app emits smartcitix:flow.external with the node and waits. The host runs whatever `ref` names on its side and posts smartcitix:flow.resume with an outcome shaped like an attempt record (at minimum { passed }). Until that message arrives the flow does not move, and nothing here assumes anything about how the host runs it.

nodes.title: Structure fire — size-up
nodes.why: The first ten minutes of a residential fire: the 360, the report on the channel, the mode called out loud and the accountability check.

nodes.title: Cardiac arrest — pit crew
nodes.why: The EMS half of the refresher: roles called on arrival, compressions that never really stop, and the swap caught before the depth goes shallow.

nodes.title: Written assessment (host)
nodes.why: The department's written assessment, which lives on the host platform. This side hands the node back and waits; the ref is an opaque string the host resolves, and this repository asserts nothing about how.

params.expects: smartcitix:flow.resume with { nodeId, outcome: { passed, stars?, seconds? } }
params.timeoutNote: There is no timeout: a flow parked on an external node stays parked until the host resumes it or an instructor restarts the flow.

nodes.title: Critical incident debrief
nodes.why: What the shift costs, four hours later: the signs named, the confidentiality rule said out loud with its limits, and the duty question kept out of the room.

nodes.title: Crew check-in
nodes.why: The crew's own check-in and the peer-support line the department uses — the close of every station in this block, and of the refresher.
